The source tree contains API request/response types, HTTP API, WebSocket gateway, CDN, WebRTC, database models, and C# admin/CDN utilities.
The README states that some incompatibilities remain and not every Discord client will connect.
Setup docs enumerate REST API, WebSocket gateway, and CDN services.
Installation docs support bare-metal npm modules, NixOS, and Docker; setup docs say Windows is not recommended.

evidence: The README identifies a reverse-engineered Linux driver for the Apple Neural Engine.
It lists ane/ as a kernel module, libane/ as a user-space library, and python/ as Python bindings.
The README says documentation is work in progress and does not give a SoC/device compatibility or test matrix.
The target is Linux with Apple Neural Engine hardware; exact supported Apple SoCs/devices are not specified in the README.
GitHub metadata reports the latest source push on 2024-03-12; repository is not archived and the releases endpoint is empty.

evidence: The README calls mkmsbr a clean-room Rust library for Microsoft-compatible MBR, FAT32 PBR, and NTFS PBR records, replacing ms-sys for supported variants.
The clean-room protocol forbids boot-code contributors from reading ms-sys source and documents reading logs, symbol checks, and similarity checks.
v1.0 scope is legacy BIOS and MBR media for Win XP/7; UEFI is out of scope.
The README reports v1.0 as shipped and an end-to-end Windows 7 install USB boot on a Dell E6410.
The status table documents real-hardware validation for MBR/FAT32 variants and identifies NTFS PBR as experimental, tested only at the L2 QEMU-smoke level.
The GitHub Releases API lists v1.0.1 (2026-05-19) and v1.0.0 (2026-05-19).
